memory_update.text: MSFT should remain a core direct candidate for this node because it combines cloud AI infrastructure, enterprise productivity distribution, developer tools, identity/security, and Copilot/agent monetization surfaces.
AMZN should remain a core cloud-platform candidate; AWS Bedrock, SageMaker, Amazon Q, and migration agents map directly to enterprise AI deployment and usage-based cloud consumption.
GOOGL should remain a core cloud AI platform candidate; Google Cloud, Gemini Enterprise, Vertex AI, TPUs, and data analytics create direct exposure to enterprise AI deployment.
CRM and NOW are likely the most direct US-listed enterprise application/workflow names for agentic AI adoption; monitor AI ARR/ACV, attach rates, renewals, and implementation ROI proof.

Important adjacent candidates not included due to the five-candidate limit: SNOW for governed enterprise data and Cortex AI, PLTR for AIP/government-commercial AI workflows, DDOG for AI observability and cost/control telemetry, MDB for operational data layer, ORCL for cloud/database/enterprise apps, ADBE for creative and marketing copilots, and HUBS/TEAM/WDAY for workflow-specific AI adoption.

NOW, SNOW, DDOG, CRWD, and PATH form a focused US-listed watchlist for enterprise-AI deployment friction: workflow/data fabric, governed data cloud, observability/cost control, identity/security, and agentic automation.
The key bottleneck signal is whether AI features increase enterprise switching costs and business-process automation, not merely whether they create higher cloud-compute expense.

Real-time data streaming is a likely sub-bottleneck for agentic workflows, but Confluent appears to have been acquired by IBM in March 2026; future passes should evaluate IBM’s Confluent integration rather than CFLT as a standalone listed equity.

Implementation services and consulting partners such as Accenture, EPAM, Globant, and large systems integrators may be second-order beneficiaries of enterprise AI deployment friction, but they were excluded from this 5-name pass to keep focus on software/control-point suppliers.
NOW, SNOW, PATH, DDOG, and ESTC should be tracked as software-layer candidates for the enterprise AI deployment-friction node, distinct from hyperscaler compute demand aggregators.
The investable chokepoint is shifting from raw model capability toward governed deployment: clean data, workflow orchestration, observability, security, cost control, and measurable ROI.

Need a later pass on cybersecurity-specific AI governance and identity control points, including ZS, CRWD, PANW, OKTA, and CYBR, because they may be adjacent chokepoints for agent authorization and data-loss prevention.
Need a later pass on CRM and application-suite incumbents such as CRM, ORCL, ADBE, INTU, and WDAY to separate true agentic workflow monetization from AI feature bundling.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the node around enterprise AI deployment friction: hyperscale cloud platforms that package AI infrastructure into enterprise services, and workflow/CRM automation platforms that turn AI into governed enterprise workflows. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Highest-priority direct exposures in this pass are Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Salesforce, and ServiceNow. Key evidence to verify next: AI-specific revenue disclosure quality, cloud gross-margin drag from AI infrastructure, Copilot/Agentforce/Now Assist seat or ACV expansion, RPO/cRPO contribution, renewal and net retention impact, and whether AI features create switching costs versus simply raising compute cost. Expanded universe around the enterprise-AI deployment-friction chokepoint: governed data, workflow orchestration, automation, observability/cost control, and security/identity. The strongest public-market mappings in this pass are not only hyperscalers, but software control points that help enterprises move AI from pilots into production while managing data silos, workflow integration, monitoring, governance, security, and ROI proof. Expanded universe for the enterprise AI deployment-friction node. The most relevant public-market mappings are not only hyperscaler compute aggregators, but software control points that sit between enterprise data, workflow systems, governance, observability, security, and ROI measurement.
